overview: A fungal leaf-spot condition associated with Alternaria species. Visual confirmation alone may not distinguish it from other apple leaf spots.
symptoms: Brown to dark leaf spots, sometimes with a purple border
Spots may enlarge and contribute to premature leaf drop
possible_causes: Alternaria species associated with apple leaf spot diseases
spread: Fungal spores may move by wind
Rain splash can contribute to movement of spores
prevention: Use locally recommended resistant or less-susceptible cultivars
Remove or manage infected debris where practical
Maintain canopy airflow
Avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness
management: Confirm the disease with local horticulture or plant-pathology guidance
Use only locally registered fungicides according to their labels
professional_help_message: Seek local advice if spotting is spreading rapidly or substantial defoliation is occurring.

overview: A broad visual category for brown leaf-spot symptoms. Several pathogens and non-infectious problems can produce similar symptoms, so the model result should be confirmed before treatment.
symptoms: Brown or dark necrotic spots on leaves
Affected leaves may yellow or fall
possible_causes: One of several fungal leaf-spot diseases
Non-infectious injury can sometimes produce similar discoloration
spread: If fungal, spores may spread through rain splash
Wind can contribute to spore movement
Infected plant debris can serve as a source of inoculum
prevention: Improve canopy airflow
Manage fallen or infected plant material
Avoid unnecessary overhead irrigation
management: Obtain local confirmation before selecting a treatment
Use only locally registered products according to their labels
professional_help_message: Consult an orchard specialist because brown-spot appearance alone does not establish the causal disease.

overview: Frogeye leaf spot is associated with the same disease complex that causes black rot on apple.
symptoms: Small circular spots with light centers
Spots may have darker purple or brown margins
Multiple spots may occur on a leaf
possible_causes: Diplodia seriata, historically reported as Botryosphaeria obtusa
favorable_conditions: Cankers or mummified fruit that can support inoculum
spread: Spores can spread from infected tissue during wet weather
prevention: Remove dead wood and mummified fruit
Prune affected material using good sanitation practices
management: Inspect the tree for cankers and fruit symptoms
professional_help_message: Request professional confirmation if cankers, fruit rot or rapid spread accompanies the leaf spots.

overview: Apple mosaic is a virus-associated condition that can produce chlorotic mosaic patterns on apple leaves.
symptoms: Cream, yellow or pale-green mosaic patterns
Irregular chlorotic bands, rings or patches on leaves
possible_causes: Apple mosaic virus or another virus associated with mosaic symptoms
favorable_conditions: Symptoms may vary with virus strain
Seasonal conditions can affect symptom expression
spread: Propagation or grafting with infected plant material is an important route
prevention: Use certified virus-tested planting and propagation material
Do not graft from symptomatic trees
Maintain clean propagation practices
professional_help_message: Consult a plant-health professional before using a suspect tree for propagation.

overview: Apple powdery mildew affects young leaves, shoots, blossoms and sometimes fruit.
symptoms: White powdery growth on leaves or shoots
Curled, narrow or stunted young leaves
spread: Airborne spores can infect developing green tissue
prevention: Use resistant cultivars when suitable
Prune heavily infected shoots where locally recommended
Maintain balanced growth
Maintain good canopy airflow
management: Begin management based on local growth-stage and disease guidance
Rotate fungicide modes of action when advised
professional_help_message: Seek orchard advice when young shoots or blossoms are extensively affected.

overview: Apple rust diseases commonly involve Gymnosporangium fungi and alternate between apple and a juniper-family host.
symptoms: Yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surfaces
Raised structures may develop on the underside of affected leaves
possible_causes: Gymnosporangium species, depending on region and symptoms
favorable_conditions: Wet spring weather during susceptible growth stages
Nearby susceptible juniper or cedar hosts
spread: Windborne spores can move between alternate hosts
prevention: Use resistant apple cultivars when appropriate
Discuss management of nearby alternate hosts with a local specialist
management: Use products only according to local labels
professional_help_message: Seek local identification because rust species and management needs can differ by region.

overview: Apple scab is a major fungal disease of apple that can affect leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Olive-green to brown leaf spots with irregular or feathered edges
favorable_conditions: Infected fallen leaves that carry inoculum
spread: Spores are released from infected leaves and lesions during suitable wet conditions
prevention: Use resistant cultivars where suitable
Promote decomposition or removal of infected fallen leaves
Improve canopy airflow
management: Use local infection-risk and growth-stage guidance
Apply only locally registered products according to labels
professional_help_message: Consult an orchard specialist when disease appears early or affects fruit production.
